headline: Hormuz Ship Incident Has Not Yet Bent Flow Count
deck: One Iranian commercial hull was reported struck near the strait, with one person dead, while an AIS monitor still showed a VLCC/ULCC outbound and daily crossings near the month-to-date pace.
body: An Iranian commercial vessel was reported struck near the Strait of Hormuz, killing one person; the physical question now is whether one logged hull incident becomes a measurable constraint on traffic through the waterway. [E1]

Public reports name the waterway and the death toll but still leave the ship name, flag, cargo and damage unresolved. Al Arabiya, citing Iranian authorities, also reported one death after the vessel was struck, so the incident is established more firmly than the cargo consequence. [E2]

The first observed flow evidence after the reported incident points to continued movement, not a shut gate: a Hormuz AIS monitor recorded OTTOMAN COURTESY outbound at 02:39 UTC after the reported 01:30 UTC event, classifying it as a 150,000-DWT VLCC/ULCC with an estimated 1.04 million barrels aboard. [E3]

By about 11:52 UTC, the same monitor showed 19 crossings in the preceding 24 hours, almost level with a September-to-date average of 19.1 a day; that does not rule out dark or jammed traffic, but it does mean the cited count has not yet shown an incident-caused drop. No source in hand names the struck cargo or ties a marine-insurance change to this incident. [E4]
